newsitem.title: USA: Milwaukee April NAPM falls to 59 from 66 in March.
newsitem.headline: Milwaukee April NAPM falls to 59 from 66 in March.

text.p: The Milwaukee chapter of the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) said on Wednesday its April business index fell to 59 from its record high of 66 in March.
The Milwaukee NAPM index stood at 52 in April 1996.
The group said the April 1997 report showed new orders, production and backlog orders fell from March levels, while supplier deliveries were unchanged.
April inventories and capital expenditures rose from March.
The report's employment components were lower, with white-collar employment down four points to 52 and blue-collar employment off a point at 61.
The report also showed average prices for 21 items fell three points to 52 from March, but remain slightly above last year's level of 51.

"We were starting to see price pressures in late fall, but now prices have plateaued," Richard Wood, a member of the Milwaukee NAPM business survey committee, said in an interview. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
